title: The Transfiguration of the Lord
short_summary: On the Transfiguration, Christ reveals his divine glory to Peter, James, and John on the mountain, strengthening them before the way of the Cross.
key_facts: The U.S. calendar keeps this feast on August 6.
The Gospels of Matthew, Mark, and Luke all record the Transfiguration.
Peter, James, and John witness Christ's face and clothes shining with glory.
Moses and Elijah appear with Jesus, and the Father's voice declares him his beloved Son.

sections.heading: Glory revealed before the Cross
sections.body: The Gospels place the Transfiguration shortly after Jesus first foretells his coming Passion. On the mountain, Peter, James, and John see his divinity shine through his humanity, a glimpse meant to strengthen them for what is to come.

sections.heading: Moses, Elijah, and the Father's voice
sections.body: Moses and Elijah appear beside Jesus, representing the Law and the Prophets, and speak with him of his coming exodus in Jerusalem. The Father's voice from the cloud declares, "This is my beloved Son; listen to him," confirming Christ's identity and authority.

sections.heading: A pledge of glory to come
sections.body: The Church has long read the Transfiguration as a preview of the glory the disciples would later see fully in the Resurrection. It shows that the road to the Cross does not contradict Christ's divine glory but leads through it to Easter.

catholic_connection_sections.heading: Listen to him
catholic_connection_sections.body: The Father's command to listen to Jesus orders the whole scene toward obedience and faith, not merely toward wonder at a vision.

catholic_connection_sections.heading: Suffering and glory held together
catholic_connection_sections.body: The feast keeps Christ's glory and his Passion together. Catholics are reminded that following Christ means walking with him through the Cross toward the glory already revealed on the mountain.
